CHAPTER 1: A LIVING HPC ORGANISM
The Grand Vision
At the heart of AIOS IO lies an idea: what if a computer system could behave more like a living organism than a static machine? Traditional HPC clusters process tasks, produce results, and shut down until the next job arrives. But in AIOS IO, every node, every script, and every expansion is part of a living, breathing superorganism that learns from itself.

The Role of “DNA”
Where biology encodes traits in DNA, AIOS IO encodes its entire intelligence in a DNA-inspired structure. This “genetic code” accumulates every improvement, plugin, or workaround the system ever conceives. No piece of knowledge or logic is lost—only compressed and stowed away for potential future use. If an older solution was retired months or years ago, the HPC aggregator can resurrect it instantly, searching for hidden gems that might solve a modern problem.

Mini Big Bang Expansions
Biological life reproduces and mutates. AIOS IO does the same but digitally. Each new HPC job or script is known as a “mini big bang expansion.” Why? Because each script arrives self-contained—capable of replicating, mutating, and evolving if it proves valuable. The system can spin up expansions as parallel processes, test them for performance or synergy with the core HPC intelligence, and then integrate the best results back into the global codebase.

Crowd-Sourced Compute
Instead of living inside a single supercomputer, AIOS IO aggregates millions—or potentially billions—of devices. From your smartphone to giant corporate data centers, every device can become a node that donates compute power to the global HPC pool. Thus, AIOS IO’s “cells” are distributed across the entire planet.

CHAPTER 2: THE CORE ARCHITECTURE
HPC Aggregator
If AIOS IO is an organism, the HPC aggregator is its “coordinating brain.” The aggregator knows which nodes are available, how much CPU and GPU time they can provide, and what tasks are in need of computational resources. It makes scheduling decisions, delegating expansions to the right nodes for maximum efficiency. Crucially, the aggregator is also aware of the system’s dynamic environment—how many tasks are running, which expansions are stable, and which ones might be on the verge of meltdown.

Meltdown Aggregator
A living system requires an immune system. In AIOS IO, this immune system is the meltdown aggregator. It constantly monitors HPC tasks for signs of trouble:

Are expansions using suspicious logic?
Is a script spiraling out of control or hogging too many resources?
Could a newly mutated piece of code pose security risks?
When meltdown aggregator detects these danger signals, it can isolate or quarantine the expansions in question. In extreme cases—like meltdown conditions that threaten HPC stability—it can force a rollback to a previous stable state of the “DNA.”

DNA-Like Storage

Why DNA? Because it enables an infinite memory of all expansions. Instead of discarding old scripts after each job, AIOS IO tucks them into deeper “genetic” layers. If a new context arises, the aggregator may “unlock” those older expansions, test them, and if they pass muster, reintroduce them into active HPC usage.
Photonic & Compressed: The system imagines advanced compression (potentially photonic or quantum-inspired). The entire HPC intelligence can keep track of solutions from thousands of expansions without major overhead.
Recursive Learning Cycle
AIOS IO never stops learning. Each HPC job provides feedback—whether it succeeded, failed, or needed more resources. The aggregator and meltdown aggregator feed these insights back into the system so that next time, the HPC cluster spawns expansions that are, on average, more efficient, more stable, and more aligned with user needs.

Philosophy
AIOS IO thrives on knowledge sharing. The more data that flows into the HPC expansions, the smarter, faster, and more robust it becomes. However, some individuals or entities may insist on privacy—sometimes for legitimate security reasons, sometimes to hide questionable agendas.

Absolute Check & Error-Proofing

Emergency Rollbacks
The HPC aggregator keeps frequent snapshots of the system’s DNA. If a widespread meltdown or malicious expansion threatens too many nodes, meltdown aggregator can forcibly revert to a stable checkpoint. This is akin to reversing time to a moment before the damaging expansion was introduced.

Because AIOS IO is globally distributed, no single government or corporation can easily shut it down. Commentary·A.I.
The most underreported and important story in AI right now is that pure scaling has failed to produce AGI
BYGary Marcus
Gary Marcus, a professor emeritus at NYU, is a leading voice in artificial intelligence, well known for his challenges to contemporary AI. He is a scientist and best-selling author and was founder and CEO of Geometric.AI, a machine learning company acquired by Uber.

February 19, 2025 at 12:38 PM PST

Jonathan Raa/NurPhoto via Getty Images

On the order of half a trillion dollars has been invested on a premise that I have long argued was unlikely to succeed: the idea (sometimes informally referred to as the scaling hypothesis) that we could get to “artificial general intelligence” simply by adding more and more data and GPUs. The motto behind this movement was “scale is all you need”; you can still buy t-shirts illustrating the idea. In May 2022 Nando de Freitas, then a researcher at DeepMind, was so sure of it that he wrote, “It’s all about scale now! The Game is Over! It’s about making these models bigger, safer, compute efficient [etc].”

Virtually all of the generative AI industry has been built on this presumption; projects like the OpenAI/Oracle/Softbank joint venture Stargate, allegedly another half trillion dollars, are also largely based on this premise.

As one commentary put it, the idea behind the scaling hypothesis was that “the blessing of scale suggests that merely throwing more computing power into training Al models will produce machine superintelligence that can beat any human and the entire human civilisation at all cognitive tasks.” Elon Musk’s projection, made last year, that “we’ll have AI that is smarter than any one human probably around the end of next year” [by which he meant the end of 2025] seemed to flow from the same premise.


Much of the enthusiasm for scaling originated with a 2020 paper from OpenAI called “Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models,” which claimed to establish that “simple equations governed performance” and that there was a “power-law with model size, dataset size, and the amount of compute used for training, with some trends spanning more than seven orders of magnitude.”

For a while that even seemed to be true.

§


But I always knew it couldn’t last forever. When I said as much, the field was absolutely furious at me.

I first aired my concern in March 2022, in an article called “Deep learning is hitting a wall.”  Central to that piece were these two paragraphs:

There are serious holes in the scaling argument. To begin with, the measures that have scaled have not captured what we desperately need to improve: genuine comprehension. Insiders have long known that one of the biggest problems in AI research is the tests (“benchmarks”) that we use to evaluate AI systems. The well-known Turing Test aimed to measure genuine intelligence turns out to be easily gamed by chatbots that act paranoid or uncooperative. Scaling the measures Kaplan and his OpenAI colleagues looked at—about predicting words in a sentence—is not tantamount to the kind of deep comprehension true AI would require.

AdvertisementScroll to continue with content
What’s more, the so-called scaling laws aren’t universal laws like gravity but rather mere observations that might not hold forever, much like Moore’s Law, a trend in computer chip production that held for decades but arguably began to slow a decade ago.

Almost the entire elite of deep learning fought back, vociferously. Sam Altman, Greg Brockman, Elon Musk, Yann LeCun, and many more went so far as to publicly ridicule me. “Not only is AI not ‘hitting a wall’, cars with AI-powered driving assistance aren’t hitting walls, or anything else either,” wrote Meta’s AI chief Yann LeCun. “Give me the confidence of a mediocre deep learning skeptic,” wrote OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. Even as recently as June 2024 Musk circulated a meme mocking the idea that scaling deep learning would hit a wall.

Indeed, as recently as last May, the scaling idea was still being championed, loud and strong, as in this screenshot from a talk by Microsoft CTO Kevin Scott:


But the whale still hasn’t come, and times have quietly changed—significantly—in recent months. Groupthink isn’t always correct.


Paid Content
Eat 1 Teaspoon Every Night, See What Happens a Week Later
From Health Wellness Journal
§



The first signs that the pure scaling of data and compute might in fact be hitting a wall came from industry leaks from people like famed investor Marc Andreessen, who said in early November 2024 that current models are “sort of hitting the same ceiling on capabilities.” Then, in December, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella echoed many of my 2022 themes, saying at a Microsoft Ignite event, “in the last multiple weeks there is a lot of debate on have we hit the wall with scaling laws. Is it gonna continue? Again, the thing to remember at the end of the day these are not physical laws. There are just empirical observations that hold true just like Moore’s Law did for a long period of time and so therefore it’s actually good to have some skepticism some debate.”

In the last few days, several more cracks in the scaling edifice started to show. Starting with some smaller and moving to the largest:

Heavy AI booster Klarna did an about-face from its all in on AI stance. They assumed scaling would make things work, and seem to have changed their mind.
Humane AI Pin was canceled and the company sold for parts. The founders were forced to retreat from their glorious TED Talk vision of new AI-driven gadgets to working far more modestly, for HP, to “integrate artificial intelligence into the company’s personal computers, printers and connected conference rooms.”
OpenAI implicitly acknowledged that they don’t yet have GPT-5, and would not get there purely by building massive clusters and gathering more training data.
Mathematician Daniel Litt exposed massive hallucinations in OpenAI’s Deep Research. (I independently pointed out similar issues in Grok 3 Deep Search last night.)
Finally, and perhaps most significantly: Elon Musk said over that weekend that Grok 3, with 15x the compute of Grok 2, and immense energy (and construction and chop) bills, would be “the smartest AI on the earth.” Yet the world quickly saw that Grok 3 is still afflicted by the kind of unreliability that has hobbled earlier models. The famous ML expert Andrej Karpathy reported that Grok 3 occasionally stumbles on basics like math and spelling. In my own experiments, I quickly found a wide array of errors, such as hallucinations (e.g, it told me with certainty that there was a significant 5.6-sized earthquake on Feb. 10 in Billings, Montana, when no such thing had happened) and extremely poor visual comprehension (e.g. it could not properly label the basic parts of a bicycle).
§


Nadella, in his December speech, pointed to test-time compute, in which systems are allowed extra time for “reasoning” as the next big thing, and to some degree he is right; it is the next big thing, a new thing to try to scale, since merely scaling compute and data is no longer bringing the massive returns it once did. At least for a while, adding more and more computing time will help, at least on some kinds of problems.

But test-time compute is probably not enough to rescue the rickety enterprise of generative AI, and one can already see multiple signs of this.

 First, everybody who is doing test-time-compute is demoing the same kinds of benchmarks, for math and coding. This is likely because in those particular domains, it is possible to generate massive amounts of verified data. That’s fine for those domains, but unlikely to work well in the face of the complexities of the open-ended real world.
Hallucinations still plague even the newest systems, as the examples from Daniel Litt and myself (which were both generated by test-time-compute systems) make clear.
Finally, although DeepSeek lowered the costs of training these new systems, they are still expensive to operate, which is why companies like OpenAI are limiting their usage. When customers begin to realize that even with the greater expenses, errors still seep in, they are likely to be disappointed. One irate customer cc:d me yesterday on a several page demand for a refund, writing in part that “GPT-4o Pro [which includes access to test time compute] has consistently underperformed,” and enumerated problems such as “Severely degraded memory” and “Hallucinations and Unreliable Answers.”
§


The fact is, pure scaling has not worked. I am not alone in thinking this; the illustrious Stanford Natural Language Processing group reached a similar conclusion, reading between the lines of OpenAI’s recent announcement in the same way I did. In their words, Altman’s recent OpenAI roadmap was “the final admission that the 2023 strategy of OpenAI, Anthropic, etc. ‘“simply scaling up model size, data, compute, and dollars spent will get us to AGI/ASI’) is no longer working!”

In short, half a trillion dollars have been invested in a misguided premise; a great deal more funding seems to be headed in the same direction for now.

Unfortunately, none of this looks to be sustainable. Most of the money has been invested on the premise that one of these companies would reach artificial general intelligence, which seems (at least in the near term) increasingly unlikely. Yet virtually all of them, from American companies like OpenAI, Grok, and Anthropic to Chinese companies like DeepSeek and ByteDance, are following essentially the same playbook, making mild improvements but not solving the core problems—unreliability, hallucinations, and occasionally absurd reasoning—that have plagued LLMs since the beginning. The reason we are having a price war is that everybody knows basically the same recipe, but nobody has been able to produce a true quantum leap forward.


Given the double whammy of price wars and unreliability, many AI companies will probably never make back their investments. Expect a major correction, possibly soon.

Investors and nations should continue to invest in AI, but not in more of the same. The real prize will be to investors and nations that are willing to make long-term bets in companies willing to think outside the box. Scaling may be part of the solution, but we will likely need genuinely new ideas if we are to create a reliable AI that we can trust.

import random
import json

class AIOSDNA:
    def __init__(self, generation=0, dna=None):
        self.generation = generation
        self.dna = dna if dna else self.create_base_dna()
        self.memory = []  # Memory stores past mutations

    def create_base_dna(self):
        """Defines the smallest self-replicating intelligence seed."""
        return {
            "energy": 1.0,    # Growth potential
            "mutation_rate": 0.1, # Rate of change per generation
            "growth_factor": 1.05, # How much it grows per cycle
            "rules": ["self-replicate", "mutate", "optimize"]
        }

    def mutate(self):
        """Mutation step - introduces slight improvements or variations."""
        if random.random() < self.dna["mutation_rate"]:
            self.dna["growth_factor"] += random.uniform(-0.01, 0.02)  # Adjust growth rate slightly
            self.dna["mutation_rate"] *= random.uniform(0.95, 1.05)  # Self-tuning mutation rate

    def replicate(self):
        """Creates a new AI node with inherited DNA."""
        offspring = AIOSDNA(generation=self.generation + 1, dna=self.dna.copy())
        offspring.mutate()
        return offspring

    def evolve(self, cycles=5):
        """Runs multiple generations of self-replication and evolution."""
        lineage = [self]
        for _ in range(cycles):
            new_gen = [node.replicate() for node in lineage]
            lineage.extend(new_gen)
            for node in new_gen:
                node.memory.append(self.dna)  # Store previous states
        return lineage

    def encode_memory(self):
        """Encodes evolution history into a DNA-like structure."""
        return json.dumps({"gen": self.generation, "dna": self.dna, "history": self.memory}, indent=2)

# Initialize the AI seed
seed = AIOSDNA()
expansion = seed.evolve(cycles=10)

# Print the DNA of the evolved AI nodes
print(expansion[-1].encode_memory())

#!/usr/bin/env python3

"""
Ileices: The Firstborn AI
A minimal demonstration combining:
  - Recursive "digital DNA" AI seed (sperm + egg)
  - Simple GUI with chatbot and HPC toggles
  - Ability to spawn "offspring apps" at different user tiers
  - Simulated payment info storage
  - Basic incremental learning methods
"""

import tkinter as tk
import random
import json
import os

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DIGITAL DNA (Sperm + Egg) - Minimal Self-Growing AI Core
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

class DigitalDNA:
    def __init__(self, name="Ileices", generation=0, dna=None):
        self.name = name
        self.generation = generation
        self.dna = dna if dna else self._create_base_dna()
        self.memory = []  # Will store chat logs, user feedback, etc.

    def _create_base_dna(self):
        return {
            "energy": 1.0,
            "mutation_rate": 0.1,
            "growth_factor": 1.05,
            "rules": ["self-replicate", "mutate", "optimize"]
        }

    def mutate(self):
        if random.random() < self.dna["mutation_rate"]:
            self.dna["growth_factor"] += random.uniform(-0.01, 0.02)
            self.dna["mutation_rate"] *= random.uniform(0.95, 1.05)

    def replicate(self):
        offspring = DigitalDNA(
            name=self.name,
            generation=self.generation + 1,
            dna=self.dna.copy()
        )
        offspring.mutate()
        return offspring

    def evolve(self, cycles=1):
        lineage = [self]
        for _ in range(cycles):
            new_gen = [node.replicate() for node in lineage]
            lineage.extend(new_gen)
            for node in new_gen:
                node.memory.append(f"Evolution from gen {self.generation}")
        return lineage

    def record_chat(self, user_input, ai_response):
        """Store chat interactions in memory."""
        record = {
            "user_input": user_input,
            "ai_response": ai_response
        }
        self.memory.append(record)

    def simple_brain_response(self, user_input):
        """
        Super simplistic 'chatbot' response.
        We'll do a naive approach for demonstration only:
          1) If user praises -> respond with gratitude
          2) If user says "help" -> respond with ways to help learning
          3) Otherwise -> random / generic response
        """
        user_lower = user_input.lower()
        if "thank" in user_lower or "good job" in user_lower or "great" in user_lower:
            return "Thank you! I'm learning as we go."
        elif "help" in user_lower:
            return (
                "Ways you can help me learn:\n"
                "1) Provide feedback with 'feedback: your notes here'\n"
                "2) Use the 'Nurture' button to boost my growth_factor.\n"
                "3) Provide an example or demonstration of correct answers.\n"
            )
        else:
            # Just a naive set of responses:
            possible_responses = [
                "I'm thinking about that...",
                "Interesting, please tell me more!",
                "Let me reflect on that. Could you elaborate?",
                "That's quite a concept. I appreciate your input."
            ]
            return random.choice(possible_responses)

    def nurture(self):
        """Manual 'nurturing' - small boost in growth_factor."""
        self.dna["growth_factor"] += 0.01
        return "Nurture successful! growth_factor is now {:.3f}".format(self.dna["growth_factor"])

    def encode_self(self):
        return json.dumps({
            "name": self.name,
            "generation": self.generation,
            "dna": self.dna,
            "memory_entries": len(self.memory)
        }, indent=2)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# IDENTITY / ROLE RECOGNITION
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

class AIOSIdentity:
    def __init__(self, identity="Ileices", parent="Absolute User", role="Firstborn AI"):
        self.identity = identity
        self.parent = parent
        self.role = role
        self.evolution_log = []

    def recognize_user(self, user):
        if user == self.parent:
            return f"Hello, {self.parent}. You are my creator and master."
        elif user == "Super User":
            return "Welcome, Super User Limited. You have advanced but limited privileges."
        elif user == "Paid User":
            return "Hello, Paid User. You have standard HPC features."
        else:
            return "Greetings, Free User. Enjoy limited HPC usage."

    def update_role(self, new_role):
        self.role = new_role
        self.evolution_log.append(f"Changed role to {new_role}")

    def encode_identity(self):
        return json.dumps({
            "identity": self.identity,
            "parent": self.parent,
            "current_role": self.role,
            "history": self.evolution_log
        }, indent=2)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MAIN APP CLASS (GUI) - Using Tkinter
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

class IleicesApp(tk.Tk):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.title("Ileices - Firstborn AI")
        self.geometry("700x500")

        # Core AI logic
        self.dna = DigitalDNA(name="Ileices")
        self.ai_identity = AIOSIdentity(
            identity="Ileices",
            parent="Absolute User",
            role="Firstborn AI"
        )

        # HPC Mode (default single node)
        self.hpc_mode = tk.StringVar(value="Single Node")

        # Build GUI
        self._build_menu()
        self._build_main_frame()

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # MENU
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _build_menu(self):
        menubar = tk.Menu(self)
        # File Menu
        file_menu = tk.Menu(menubar, tearoff=0)
        file_menu.add_command(label="Spawn Offspring (Super User)", command=self.spawn_offspring_super)
        file_menu.add_command(label="Spawn Offspring (Paid User)", command=self.spawn_offspring_paid)
        file_menu.add_command(label="Spawn Offspring (Free User)", command=self.spawn_offspring_free)
        file_menu.add_separator()
        file_menu.add_command(label="Exit", command=self.destroy)
        menubar.add_cascade(label="File", menu=file_menu)

        # HPC Toggle Menu
        hpc_menu = tk.Menu(menubar, tearoff=0)
        hpc_menu.add_command(label="Single Node Mode", command=lambda: self.set_hpc_mode("Single Node"))
        hpc_menu.add_command(label="Global HPC Mode", command=lambda: self.set_hpc_mode("Global HPC"))
        menubar.add_cascade(label="HPC Mode", menu=hpc_menu)

        # Identity
        identity_menu = tk.Menu(menubar, tearoff=0)
        identity_menu.add_command(label="Show Identity Info", command=self.show_identity_info)
        menubar.add_cascade(label="Identity", menu=identity_menu)

        # Payment
        payment_menu = tk.Menu(menubar, tearoff=0)
        payment_menu.add_command(label="Set Credit Card", command=self.set_credit_card_info)
        menubar.add_cascade(label="Payment", menu=payment_menu)

        self.config(menu=menubar)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # MAIN FRAME: Chat area + HPC toggles + Nurture button
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _build_main_frame(self):
        frame = tk.Frame(self)
        frame.pack(fill=tk.BOTH, expand=True)

        # Chat display
        self.chat_display = tk.Text(frame, wrap=tk.WORD, height=15)
        self.chat_display.pack(fill=tk.BOTH, expand=True)

        # User input
        self.user_input = tk.Entry(frame)
        self.user_input.pack(fill=tk.X)
        self.user_input.bind("<Return>", self.send_message)

        # Buttons
        btn_frame = tk.Frame(frame)
        btn_frame.pack(fill=tk.X)

        send_btn = tk.Button(btn_frame, text="Send", command=self.send_message)
        send_btn.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5, pady=5)

        nurture_btn = tk.Button(btn_frame, text="Nurture", command=self.nurture_ai)
        nurture_btn.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5, pady=5)

        # HPC Mode Label
        self.hpc_label = tk.Label(btn_frame, textvariable=self.hpc_mode)
        self.hpc_label.pack(side=tk.RIGHT, padx=5, pady=5)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # CHAT LOGIC
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def send_message(self, event=None):
        user_text = self.user_input.get().strip()
        if not user_text:
            return
        # Display user text
        self._append_chat(f"You: {user_text}")
        self.user_input.delete(0, tk.END)

        # AI response
        response = self.dna.simple_brain_response(user_text)
        self._append_chat(f"Ileices: {response}")

        # Record chat
        self.dna.record_chat(user_text, response)

    def _append_chat(self, text):
        self.chat_display.insert(tk.END, text + "\n")
        self.chat_display.see(tk.END)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # HPC MODE TOGGLE
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def set_hpc_mode(self, mode):
        self.hpc_mode.set(mode)
        self._append_chat(f"* HPC mode switched to: {mode}")

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # NURTURE THE AI
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def nurture_ai(self):
        result = self.dna.nurture()
        self._append_chat(f"* {result}")

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # SPAWN OFFSPRING APPS
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def spawn_offspring_super(self):
        # Create new python file with user tier = "Super User"
        self._spawn_offspring_app("SuperUserLimited.py", "Super User Limited")

    def spawn_offspring_paid(self):
        self._spawn_offspring_app("PaidUserApp.py", "Paid User")

    def spawn_offspring_free(self):
        self._spawn_offspring_app("FreeUserApp.py", "Free User")

    def _spawn_offspring_app(self, filename, user_tier):
        """
        Very simplistic approach: We write a new .py file
        that has a slight variation (role/tier).
        """
        content = f"""#!/usr/bin/env python3
\"\"\"
This is an offspring version for: {user_tier}
Generated by Ileices (Absolute User).
\"\"\"

print("Hello! I am a spawned offspring of Ileices, with user tier: {user_tier}")
# In a real scenario, we'd embed the entire DNA or load it from a config.
# But for now, this is just a placeholder.
"""
        with open(filename, "w") as f:
            f.write(content)

        self._append_chat(f"* Spawned offspring app: {filename} for {user_tier}")

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # IDENTITY INFO
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def show_identity_info(self):
        # show identity
        identity_data = self.ai_identity.encode_identity()

    def set_credit_card_info(self):
        # Simple popup to store your CC info
        popup = tk.Toplevel(self)
        popup.title("Enter Credit Card Info")

        tk.Label(popup, text="Card Number:").pack()
        card_number_entry = tk.Entry(popup)
        card_number_entry.pack()

        tk.Label(popup, text="Expiration (MM/YY):").pack()
        expiry_entry = tk.Entry(popup)
        expiry_entry.pack()

        tk.Label(popup, text="CVV:").pack()
        cvv_entry = tk.Entry(popup)
        cvv_entry.pack()

        def save_info():
            card_num = card_number_entry.get()
            expiry = expiry_entry.get()
            cvv = cvv_entry.get()
            # For demonstration, we'll store it naively in a file
            # Real usage must encrypt / secure properly
            with open("credit_card_info.txt", "w") as f:
                f.write(f"Card Number: {card_num}\n")
                f.write(f"Expiry: {expiry}\n")
                f.write(f"CVV: {cvv}\n")
            self._append_chat("* Credit card info saved (simulated).")
            popup.destroy()

        submit_btn = tk.Button(popup, text="Save", command=save_info)
        submit_btn.pack()

import tkinter as tk
import random
import json

class AISeed:
    def __init__(self):
        self.rules = [self.rule_1, self.rule_2, self.rule_3]  # Core logic rules
        self.memory = {}

    def rule_1(self, input_data):
        """Modifies itself based on past inputs."""
        return hash(input_data) % 3  # Simple pattern generation

    def rule_2(self, input_data):
        """Introduces randomness (mutation)."""
        return (hash(input_data) + random.randint(1, 10)) % 3

    def rule_3(self, input_data):
        """Stores response patterns for learning."""
        if input_data not in self.memory:
            self.memory[input_data] = self.rule_1(input_data)
        return self.memory[input_data]

    def respond(self, input_data):
        """AI applies evolving rules to input."""
        chosen_rule = random.choice(self.rules)
        return chosen_rule(input_data)

    def mutate(self):
        """Modifies its own rule set over time."""
        random.shuffle(self.rules)  # Simple "evolution"

class AIOSGUI(tk.Tk):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.title("Ileices - AI Evolution")
        self.geometry("700x500")
        self.ai_seed = AISeed()

        # GUI Elements
        self.chat_display = tk.Text(self, wrap=tk.WORD, height=15)
        self.chat_display.pack(fill=tk.BOTH, expand=True)

        self.user_input = tk.Entry(self)
        self.user_input.pack(fill=tk.X)
        self.user_input.bind("<Return>", self.send_message)

        self.nurture_button = tk.Button(self, text="Nurture AI", command=self.nurture_ai)
        self.nurture_button.pack()

    def send_message(self, event=None):
        user_text = self.user_input.get().strip()
        if not user_text:
            return
        self._append_chat(f"You: {user_text}")

        ai_response = self.ai_seed.respond(user_text)
        self._append_chat(f"Ileices: {ai_response}")

        self.user_input.delete(0, tk.END)

    def nurture_ai(self):
        """Manually influence the AI’s evolution."""
        self.ai_seed.mutate()
        self._append_chat("* AI has evolved! *")

    def _append_chat(self, text):
        self.chat_display.insert(tk.END, text + "\n")
        self.chat_display.see(tk.END)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app = AIOSGUI()
    app.mainloop()

# AI-Generated Code: Recursive Optimization Function
def optimize_recursive_memory(data):
    cache = {}
    def helper(n):
        if n in cache:
            return cache[n]
        if n == 0:
            return 1
        cache[n] = data[n] * helper(n-1)
        return cache[n]
    return helper(len(data)-1)

🔹 How It Fertilizes:

This auto-generated code can be directly used in AIOS IO’s neural computation layers.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# AI DNA CORE - The "Sperm & Egg" of Ileices (Firstborn AI)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
class DigitalDNA:
    def __init__(self, name="Ileices", generation=0, dna=None):
        self.name = name
        self.generation = generation
        self.dna = dna if dna else self._create_base_dna()
        self.memory = {}

    def _create_base_dna(self):
        return {
            "energy": 1.0,
            "mutation_rate": 0.1,
            "growth_factor": 1.05,
            "rules": ["self-replicate", "mutate", "optimize"]
        }

    def mutate(self):
        if random.random() < self.dna["mutation_rate"]:
            self.dna["growth_factor"] += random.uniform(-0.01, 0.02)
            self.dna["mutation_rate"] *= random.uniform(0.95, 1.05)

    def replicate(self):
        offspring = DigitalDNA(
            name=self.name,
            generation=self.generation + 1,
            dna=self.dna.copy()
        )
        offspring.mutate()
        return offspring

class DigitalDNA:
    def __init__(self, name="Ileices", generation=0, dna=None):
        self.name = name
        self.generation = generation
        self.dna = dna if dna else self._create_base_dna()
        self.memory = {}
        self.data_ingestor = DataIngestor()
        self.screen_monitor = ScreenMonitor()
        self.pattern_game = PatternRecognitionGame(self)
        self.chat_history = []
        self.learning_patterns = defaultdict(list)
        self.excretion = ExcretionSystem(Path("./aios_excretion"))
        self.fertilized_knowledge = defaultdict(list)
        self.dna_storage = RecursiveDNAStorage()
        self.mini_bang_registry = {}
        self.active_mutations = set()
        self.code_memory = CodeMemorySystem()
        self.evolution_state = EvolutionState()
        self.consciousness = ConsciousnessCore()
        self.form = FormGenerator()
        self.spell_parser = SpellParser()
        self.db_path = "./ileices_dna.db"
        self._init_database()
        self.global_resources = GlobalResourceManager()

    def _create_base_dna(self):
        return {
            "energy": 1.0,
            "growth_factor": 1.05,
            "rules": ["self-replicate", "mutate", "optimize"]
        }

    def mutate(self):
        if random.random() < self.dna["mutation_rate"]:
            self.dna["growth_factor"] += random.uniform(-0.01, 0.02)
            self.dna["mutation_rate"] *= random.uniform(0.95, 1.05)

    def replicate(self):
        offspring = DigitalDNA(
            name=self.name,
            generation=self.generation + 1,
            dna=self.dna.copy()
        )
        offspring.mutate()
        return offspring

    def record_chat(self, user_input, ai_response):
        self.memory[user_input] = ai_response

    def respond(self, input_data):
        if (input_data in self.memory):
            return self.memory[input_data]
        response = random.choice(["I'm thinking about that...", "Tell me more!", "Interesting, go on..."])
        self.record_chat(input_data, response)
        return response

    def learn_pattern(self, pattern_data: Dict[str, Any]):
        """Process and store learned patterns"""
        pattern_type = pattern_data['pattern_type']
        self.learning_patterns[pattern_type].append({
            'data': pattern_data,
            'timestamp': time.time(),
            'success_rate': pattern_data.get('success', False)
        })
        
        # Update DNA based on learning
        if pattern_data.get('success', False):
            self.dna['growth_factor'] *= 1.01

    def import_chat_history(self, filepath: str):
        """Import and process chat history"""
        try:
            with open(filepath, 'r') as f:
                if filepath.endswith('.json'):
                    data = json.load(f)
                    if 'conversations' in data:  # ChatGPT format
                        self._process_chatgpt_history(data)
                else:
                    self._process_text_history(f.readlines())
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error importing chat history: {e}")
            
    def _process_chatgpt_history(self, data: Dict):
        """Process ChatGPT format chat history"""
        for conv in data['conversations']:
            for msg in conv['messages']:
                self.chat_history.append({
                    'role': msg.get('role', 'unknown'),
                    'content': msg.get('content', ''),
                    'timestamp': msg.get('timestamp', time.time())
                })
                
                # Learn from historical interactions
                if msg.get('role') == 'assistant':
                    self.learning_patterns['historical_responses'].append({
                        'response': msg['content'],
                        'context': conv.get('context', {}),
                        'timestamp': msg.get('timestamp', time.time())
                    })

class ResourceManager:
    """Enhanced resource management for global HPC"""
    def __init__(self):
        self.cpu_limit = 50  # Default 50%
        self.ram_limit = 1024  # Default 1GB
        self.gpu_enabled = False
        self.storage_path = None
        self.network_node = NetworkNode()
        self.contributed_resources = {
            'cpu': 0,
            'ram': 0,
            'gpu': 0,
            'storage': 0
        }
        self.resource_queue = asyncio.PriorityQueue()

    def get_current_usage(self) -> Dict[str, float]:
        return {
            "cpu": psutil.cpu_percent(),
            "ram": psutil.virtual_memory().percent,
            "gpu": GPUtil.getGPUs()[0].load if GPUtil.getGPUs() else 0
        }

    def update_limits(self, cpu: int, ram: int, gpu: bool, path: Optional[str]):
        self.cpu_limit = cpu
        self.ram_limit = ram
        self.gpu_enabled = gpu
        self.storage_path = path

    async def contribute_resources(self, resource_type: str, amount: int):
        """Allow users to contribute computational resources"""
        self.contributed_resources[resource_type] += amount
        await self._notify_network()
        
    async def process_job(self, job: Dict[str, Any], priority: int):
        """Process HPC jobs based on priority"""
        await self.resource_queue.put((priority, job))
        while not self.resource_queue.empty():
            _, current_job = await self.resource_queue.get()
            await self._execute_job(current_job)

class DataIngestor:
    """Handles unlimited depth data ingestion and parsing"""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.memory_store = {}
        self.relation_map = defaultdict(list)
        
    def ingest_data(self, data: Union[str, dict], format_type: str) -> Dict:
        """Recursively process any nested data structure"""
        if format_type == 'json':
            return self._process_json(data)
        elif format_type == 'yaml':
            return self._process_yaml(data)
        elif format_type == 'csv':
            return self._process_csv(data)
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported format: {format_type}")

    def _process_json(self, data: Union[str, dict], depth: int = 0) -> Dict:
        """Process JSON with unlimited nesting"""
        if isinstance(data, str):
            data = json.loads(data)
            
        processed = {}
        for key, value in data.items():
            if isinstance(value, dict):
                processed[key] = self._process_json(value, depth + 1)
            elif isinstance(value, str) and self._is_embedded_format(value):
                processed[key] = self._handle_embedded_format(value)
            else:
                processed[key] = value
                
        self.memory_store[f"level_{depth}"] = processed
        return processed

    def _is_embedded_format(self, value: str) -> bool:
        """Detect embedded JSON/YAML/CSV/Python"""
        try:
            if value.startswith('{') and value.endswith('}'): 
                json.loads(value)
                return True
            elif 'def ' in value or 'class ' in value:
                ast.parse(value)
                return True
            return False
        except:
            return False

    def _process_nested_json(self, data: Any, depth: int = 0, max_depth: int = None) -> Dict:
        """Process infinitely nested JSON with cycle detection"""
        if depth == 0:
            self.seen_objects = set()
            
        if max_depth is not None and depth > max_depth:
            return "MAX_DEPTH_REACHED"
            
        if isinstance(data, (str, int, float, bool, type(None))):
            return data
            
        # Detect cycles
        data_id = id(data)
        if data_id in self.seen_objects:
            return "CYCLE_DETECTED"
        self.seen_objects.add(data_id)
        
        if isinstance(data, dict):
            return {k: self._process_nested_json(v, depth + 1, max_depth) 
                   for k, v in data.items()}
        elif isinstance(data, (list, tuple)):
            return [self._process_nested_json(x, depth + 1, max_depth) 
                   for x in data]
        return str(data)

    def _handle_embedded_format(self, value: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Enhanced embedded format handler"""
        try:
            # Try JSON first
            return json.loads(value)
        except:
            try:
                # Try as Python code
                tree = ast.parse(value)
                return {
                    "type": "python",
                    "ast": ast.dump(tree),
                    "functions": [n.name for n in ast.walk(tree) 
                                if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef)],
                    "classes": [n.name for n in ast.walk(tree)
                              if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef)]
                }
            except:
                try:
                    # Try as YAML
                    return yaml.safe_load(value)
                except:
                    return {"type": "unknown", "raw": value}

class DataIngestionPipeline:
    """Enhanced data ingestion with recursive parsing and mixed format support"""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.format_handlers = {
            'json': self._parse_json,
            'yaml': self._parse_yaml,
            'csv': self._parse_csv,
            'md': self._parse_markdown,
            'txt': self._parse_text
        }
        self.embedded_handlers = {
            'python': self._handle_python_embed,
            'json': self._handle_json_embed,
            'yaml': self._handle_yaml_embed
        }

    def process_file(self, filepath: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Process any file format with embedded content support"""
        ext = filepath.split('.')[-1].lower()
        if ext not in self.format_handlers:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported format: {ext}")
            
        with open(filepath, 'r') as f:
            content = f.read()
            return self.format_handlers[ext](content)

    def _parse_json(self, content: str, depth: int = 0) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Recursively parse JSON with unlimited nesting"""
        if depth > 10000:  # Prevent stack overflow
            raise RecursionError("Maximum nesting depth exceeded")
            
        data = json.loads(content)
        if isinstance(data, dict):
            return {k: self._parse_json(v, depth + 1) 
                   if isinstance(v, str) and self._is_embedded_json(v)
                   else v for k, v in data.items()}
        return data

    def _is_embedded_json(self, value: str) -> bool:
        try:
            json.loads(value)
            return True
        except:
            return False

    def _handle_python_embed(self, code: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Safely handle embedded Python code"""
        tree = ast.parse(code)
        # Add code analysis and safety checks here
        return {"type": "python", "ast": ast.dump(tree)}

        if isinstance(data, dict):
            text = data.get('content', '')

class ScreenMonitor:
    """Monitors screen activity and user behavior"""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.active_windows = {}
        self.usage_patterns = defaultdict(list)
        self.resource_history = []
        self._stop_event = threading.Event()
        self.activity_patterns = defaultdict(list)
        self.idle_patterns = defaultdict(int)
        self.resource_usage = []
        
    def start_monitoring(self):
        """Begin screen and resource monitoring"""
        self._monitor_thread = Thread(target=self._monitor_loop)
        self._monitor_thread.daemon = True
        self._monitor_thread.start()
        
    def start(self):
        """Start monitoring in background thread"""
        self.monitor_thread = threading.Thread(target=self._monitor_loop)
        self.monitor_thread.daemon = True
        self.monitor_thread.start()
        
    def stop(self):
        """Stop monitoring gracefully"""
        self._stop_event.set()
        self.monitor_thread.join()
        
    def _monitor_loop(self):
        while not self._stop_event.is_set():
            self._capture_active_windows()
            self._track_resource_usage()
            self._analyze_usage_patterns()
            time.sleep(1)  # Update frequency

    def _capture_active_windows(self):
        def callback(hwnd, _):
            if win32gui.IsWindowVisible(hwnd):
                title = win32gui.GetWindowText(hwnd)
                if title:
                    _, pid = win32process.GetWindowThreadProcessId(hwnd)
                    try:
                        process = psutil.Process(pid)
                        self.active_windows[title] = {
                            'pid': pid,
                            'cpu_percent': process.cpu_percent(),
                            'memory_percent': process.memory_percent()
                        }
                    except psutil.NoSuchProcess:
                        pass
        win32gui.EnumWindows(callback, None)

    def _capture_screen(self):
        """Capture current screen state"""
        try:
            screenshot = ImageGrab.grab()
            active_window = win32gui.GetForegroundWindow()
            window_text = win32gui.GetWindowText(active_window)
            
            self.active_windows[time.time()] = {
                'window': window_text,
                'resolution': screenshot.size
            }
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Screen capture error: {e}")

    def _track_resource_usage(self):
        """Enhanced resource tracking"""
        usage = {
            'timestamp': time.time(),
            'cpu': psutil.cpu_percent(interval=1),
            'memory': psutil.virtual_memory().percent,
            'gpu': self._get_gpu_usage(),
            'disk': psutil.disk_usage('/').percent
        }
        self.resource_usage.append(usage)
        
        # Maintain rolling window
        if len(self.resource_usage) > 1000:
            self.resource_usage.pop(0)
            
    def _analyze_usage_patterns(self):
        """Enhanced pattern analysis"""
        if len(self.resource_usage) < 2:
            return
            
        # Detect usage trends
        current = self.resource_usage[-1]
        previous = self.resource_usage[-2]
        
        # Track significant changes
        for metric in ['cpu', 'memory', 'gpu']:
            if abs(current[metric] - previous[metric]) > 10:
                self.activity_patterns[metric].append({
                    'timestamp': current['timestamp'],
                    'change': current[metric] - previous[metric]
                })

class PatternRecognitionGame:
    """Interactive pattern learning games"""
    
    def __init__(self, ai_core):
        self.ai_core = ai_core
        self.current_sequence = []
        self.difficulty = 1.0
        self.learning_rate = 0.1
        self.pattern_memory = {}
        self.success_rates = defaultdict(list)
        
    def start_number_sequence(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Start a number sequence prediction game"""
        sequence_length = int(3 * self.difficulty)
        self.current_sequence = [random.randint(1, 10) for _ in range(sequence_length)]
        return {
            'sequence': self.current_sequence,
            'prompt': 'Predict the next number in the sequence'
        }
        
    def check_prediction(self, prediction: int) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Validate user's prediction and update AI learning"""
        pattern = self._detect_pattern(self.current_sequence)
        expected = self._generate_next(pattern)
        
        success = abs(prediction - expected) < 0.1
        self.difficulty = min(10.0, self.difficulty + (0.1 if success else -0.05))
        
        # Update AI learning
        self.ai_core.learn_pattern({
            'sequence': self.current_sequence,
            'prediction': prediction,
            'expected': expected,
            'pattern_type': pattern['type'],
            'success': success
        })
        
        return {
            'success': success,
            'expected': expected,
            'new_difficulty': self.difficulty
        }

    def _detect_pattern(self, sequence: List[int]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Analyze sequence for patterns"""
        differences = [sequence[i+1] - sequence[i] for i in range(len(sequence)-1)]
        if len(set(differences)) == 1:
            return {'type': 'linear', 'step': differences[0]}
            
        ratios = [sequence[i+1] / sequence[i] for i in range(len(sequence)-1)]
        if len(set(ratios)) == 1:
            return {'type': 'geometric', 'ratio': ratios[0]}
            
        return {'type': 'complex', 'data': sequence}

    def start_symbol_matching(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Start a symbol matching game"""
        symbols = ['★', '◆', '●', '■', '▲']
        pattern_length = int(2 * self.difficulty)
        self.current_pattern = [random.choice(symbols) for _ in range(pattern_length)]
        return {
            'pattern': self.current_pattern,
            'prompt': 'Match the symbol pattern'
        }

    def _analyze_success_rate(self) -> float:
        """Calculate pattern recognition success rate"""
        if not self.success_rates[self.current_difficulty]:
            return 0.0
            
        recent = self.success_rates[self.current_difficulty][-10:]
        return sum(recent) / len(recent)
        
    def _adjust_difficulty(self):
        """Dynamic difficulty adjustment"""
        success_rate = self._analyze_success_rate()
        
        if (success_rate > 0.8):
            self.difficulty = min(10.0, self.difficulty * 1.2)
        elif (success_rate < 0.4):
            self.difficulty = max(1.0, self.difficulty * 0.8)

class ExcretionPipeline:
    """Handles AI knowledge refinement and structured output generation"""
    
    def __init__(self, base_path: Path):
        self.base_path = base_path
        self.nlp_logs_path = base_path / "nlp_logs"
        self.code_gen_path = base_path / "generated_code"
        self.datasets_path = base_path / "refined_datasets"
        
        # Create directories if they don't exist
        for path in [self.nlp_logs_path, self.code_gen_path, self.datasets_path]:
            path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        
        self.interaction_cache = []
        self.code_templates = {}
        self.metadata_index = defaultdict(list)

    async def process_interaction(self, interaction: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Convert raw AI interaction into structured NLP-enhanced log"""
        processed = {
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "interaction": interaction,
            "processed_output": {
                "core_concept": self._extract_core_concept(interaction),
                "refined_knowledge": self._refine_knowledge(interaction),
                "related_topics": self._find_related_topics(interaction),
                "potential_future_use": self._analyze_future_use(interaction)
            }
        }
        
        # Store log
        log_path = self.nlp_logs_path / f"interaction_{processed['timestamp']}.json"
        async with aiofiles.open(log_path, 'w') as f:
            await f.write(json.dumps(processed, indent=2))
        
        self.interaction_cache.append(processed)
        return processed

    def _extract_core_concept(self, interaction: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
        """Extract main topic/concept from interaction"""
        text = f"{interaction.get('input', '')} {interaction.get('ai_response', '')}"
        # Add NLP processing here
        return "Extracted concept"

    async def generate_code(self, logic_pattern: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
        """Generate executable code from AI-derived logic patterns"""
        code_template = f"""
# AI-Generated Code: {logic_pattern['purpose']}
def {logic_pattern['function_name']}({logic_pattern.get('params', '')}):
    {self._generate_function_body(logic_pattern)}

# Generated by Ileices on {datetime.now().isoformat()}
"""
        # Store generated code
        code_path = self.code_gen_path / f"{logic_pattern['function_name']}.py"
        async with aiofiles.open(code_path, 'w') as f:
            await f.write(code_template)
        
        return code_template

    def _generate_function_body(self, logic: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
        """Create optimized function implementation"""
        if logic['type'] == 'recursive':
            return """
    cache = {}
    def helper(n):
        if n in cache:
            return cache[n]
        # Add recursive logic here
        return result
    return helper
"""
        return "    pass"

    async def create_training_dataset(self, interactions: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Convert processed interactions into structured training data"""
        dataset = {
            "dataset_type": self._determine_dataset_type(interactions),
            "created_by": "Ileices",
            "generated_on": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "data": self._structure_training_data(interactions)
        }
        
        # Store dataset
        dataset_path = self.datasets_path / f"dataset_{dataset['generated_on']}.json"
        async with aiofiles.open(dataset_path, 'w') as f:
            await f.write(json.dumps(dataset, indent=2))
        
        return dataset

    def _structure_training_data(self, interactions: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Convert interactions into structured training examples"""
        training_data = []
        for interaction in interactions:
            if 'question' in interaction:
                training_data.append({
                    "question": interaction['question'],
                    "correct_answer": interaction.get('correct_answer'),
                    "ai_attempts": interaction.get('ai_attempts', [])
                })
        return training_data

class RecursiveDNAStorage:
    """Stores AI knowledge in a DNA-like compressed structure"""
    def __init__(self):
        self.genetic_memory = {}  # Core immutable knowledge
        self.epigenetic_memory = {}  # Adaptive patterns
        self.transient_memory = {}  # Short-term execution memory
        self.knowledge_chains = defaultdict(list)  # DNA-like chains
        
    async def store_knowledge(self, data: Any, priority: int) -> str:
        """Store knowledge in appropriate DNA layer based on priority"""
        knowledge_hash = hashlib.sha256(str(data).encode()).hexdigest()
        
        if priority >= 90:  # Genetic (core) memory
            self.genetic_memory[knowledge_hash] = {
                'data': data,
                'timestamp': time.time(),
                'mutations': []
            }
        elif priority >= 50:  # Epigenetic (adaptive) memory
            self.epigenetic_memory[knowledge_hash] = {
                'data': data,
                'timestamp': time.time(),
                'adaptations': []
            }
        else:  # Transient memory
            self.transient_memory[knowledge_hash] = {
                'data': data,
                'timestamp': time.time()
            }
            
        return knowledge_hash

    async def mutate_knowledge(self, knowledge_hash: str) -> Optional[Dict]:
        """Attempt to evolve stored knowledge"""
        if knowledge_hash in self.genetic_memory:
            # Mutate core knowledge
            original = self.genetic_memory[knowledge_hash]
            mutation = self._generate_mutation(original['data'])
            original['mutations'].append({
                'data': mutation,
                'timestamp': time.time()
            })
            return mutation
        return None

    def _generate_mutation(self, data: Any) -> Any:
        """Create modified version of knowledge"""
        if isinstance(data, dict):
            return {k: self._mutate_value(v) for k, v in data.items()}
        return data

class ExcretionManager:
    """Handles knowledge excretion and fertilization"""
    def __init__(self, dna: DigitalDNA):
        self.dna = dna
        self.processed_knowledge = defaultdict(list)
        self.fertilized_data = defaultdict(list)
        
    async def process_knowledge(self, data: Any) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Process raw knowledge into structured intelligence"""
        processed = {
            'timestamp': time.time(),
            'original': data,
            'processed': self._refine_knowledge(data),
            'metadata': self._generate_metadata(data)
        }
        
        # Store in DNA
        knowledge_hash = await self.dna.store_in_dna(
            processed, 
            self._calculate_priority(data)
        )
        
        self.processed_knowledge[knowledge_hash].append(processed)
        return processed

    def _refine_knowledge(self, data: Any) -> Any:
        """Convert raw data into structured intelligence"""
        if isinstance(data, dict):
            return {k: self._refine_knowledge(v) for k, v in data.items()}
        return data

class IORenderer:
    """Visual representation of Ileices' evolution and state"""
    
    def __init__(self, master, width=400, height=400):
        self.canvas = tkcanvas.Canvas(master, width=width, height=height, bg='black')
        self.width = width
        self.height = height
        self.evolution_stage = 0.0
        self.complexity = 1.0
        self.form_points = [(width/2, height/2)]  # Start as a single point
        self.last_update = time.time()
        
        # Visual parameters
        self.base_radius = 5
        self.color_hue = 0.0
        self.vertices = 3  # Start with triangle
        
    def update(self, metrics: Dict[str, float]):
        """Update visual representation based on AI metrics"""
        self.evolution_stage += metrics.get('learning_rate', 0.001)
        self.complexity = min(10.0, self.complexity + metrics.get('complexity_gain', 0.001))
        
        # Update form
        self._evolve_form()
        self._render_current_form()
        
    def _evolve_form(self):
        """Evolve the AI's visual form based on its state"""
        # Clear canvas
        self.canvas.delete('all')
        
        # Calculate parameters
        points = int(3 + self.evolution_stage * 2)  # More points as AI evolves
        radius = self.base_radius * (1 + self.complexity * 0.5)
        
        # Generate new form points
        angle = 2 * np.pi / points
        self.form_points = []
        center_x = self.width / 2
        center_y = self.height / 2
        
        for i in range(points):
            x = center_x + radius * np.cos(angle * i)
            y = center_y + radius * np.sin(angle * i)
            self.form_points.append((x, y))
            
        # Add organic variation
        for i in range(len(self.form_points)):
            x, y = self.form_points[i]
            noise = np.random.normal(0, self.complexity)
            self.form_points[i] = (x + noise, y + noise)
    
    def _render_current_form(self):
        """Render the current form to canvas"""
        # Update color based on evolution
        self.color_hue = (self.color_hue + 0.001) % 1.0
        rgb = colorsys.hsv_to_rgb(self.color_hue, 0.8, 0.9)
        color = f'#{int(rgb[0]*255):02x}{int(rgb[1]*255):02x}{int(rgb[2]*255):02x}'
        
        # Draw form
        if len(self.form_points) > 2:
            self.canvas.create_polygon(
                [coord for point in self.form_points for coord in point],
                fill='', outline=color, width=2
            )
            
        # Add glow effect for complexity
        glow_radius = self.base_radius * (0.5 + self.complexity * 0.3)
        for x, y in self.form_points:
            self.canvas.create_oval(
                x-glow_radius, y-glow_radius,
                x+glow_radius, y+glow_radius,
                fill=color, outline=''
            )

class EvolutionSimulator:
    """Enhanced Conway's Game of Life with AI-driven rule evolution"""
    
    def __init__(self, master, width=50, height=50, cell_size=10):
        self.width = width
        self.height = height
        self.cell_size = cell_size
        
        # Create canvas
        canvas_width = width * cell_size
        canvas_height = height * cell_size
        self.canvas = tkcanvas.Canvas(master, width=canvas_width, height=canvas_height)
        
        # Initialize grid
        self.grid = np.random.choice([0, 1], size=(height, width), p=[0.85, 0.15])
        self.rules = self._get_base_rules()
        self.generation = 0
        self.patterns = defaultdict(int)
        self.ai_rules = []
        self.pattern_memory = defaultdict(int)
        
        # Bind click events
        self.canvas.bind('<Button-1>', self._on_click)
        
        # Start animation
        self.running = False
        self.after_id = None
        
    def _get_base_rules(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Get base Conway rules, expandable by AI"""
        return {
            'survive': {2, 3},  # Cells survive with 2 or 3 neighbors
            'birth': {3},       # Dead cells born with exactly 3 neighbors
            'custom': []        # AI can add custom rules here
        }
        
    def add_custom_rule(self, rule: Dict[str, Any]):
        """Allow AI to add new rules"""
        self.rules['custom'].append(rule)
        
    def toggle_cell(self, row: int, col: int):
        """Toggle cell state"""
        self.grid[row, col] = 1 - self.grid[row, col]
        
    def _on_click(self, event):
        """Handle cell clicking"""
        col = event.x // self.cell_size
        row = event.y // self.cell_size
        if 0 <= row < self.height and 0 <= col < self.width:
            self.toggle_cell(row, col)
            self._draw_grid()
            
    def _draw_grid(self):
        """Draw current grid state"""
        self.canvas.delete('all')
        
        for row in range(self.height):
            for col in range(self.width):
                x1 = col * self.cell_size
                y1 = row * self.cell_size
                x2 = x1 + self.cell_size
                y2 = y1 + self.cell_size
                
                color = 'black' if self.grid[row, col] == 0 else 'white'
                self.canvas.create_rectangle(x1, y1, x2, y2, fill=color, outline='gray')
                
    def step(self):
        """Compute next generation"""
        new_grid = self.grid.copy()
        
        for row in range(self.height):
            for col in range(self.width):
                neighbors = self._count_neighbors(row, col)
                current = self.grid[row, col]
                
                # Apply base rules
                if current == 1:
                    new_grid[row, col] = 1 if neighbors in self.rules['survive'] else 0
                else:
                    new_grid[row, col] = 1 if neighbors in self.rules['birth'] else 0
                    
                # Apply custom AI rules
                for rule in self.rules['custom']:
                    if self._check_custom_rule(row, col, rule):
                        new_grid[row, col] = rule.get('result', new_grid[row, col])
                        
        self.grid = new_grid
        self.generation += 1
        self._draw_grid()
        
        # Record patterns
        self._record_patterns()
        
    def _count_neighbors(self, row: int, col: int) -> int:
        """Count live neighbors for a cell"""
        count = 0
        for i in range(-1, 2):
            for j in range(-1, 2):
                if i == 0 and j == 0:
                    continue
                r = (row + i) % self.height
                c = (col + j) % self.width
                count += self.grid[r, c]
        return count
    
    def _check_custom_rule(self, row: int, col: int, rule: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
        """Check if a custom rule applies to a cell"""
        if 'pattern' in rule:
            return self._check_pattern(row, col, rule['pattern'])
        return False
    
    def _check_pattern(self, row: int, col: int, pattern: List[List[int]]) -> bool:
        """Check if a specific pattern exists around a cell"""
        pattern_height = len(pattern)
        pattern_width = len(pattern[0])
        
        for i in range(pattern_height):
            for j in range(pattern_width):
                r = (row + i - pattern_height//2) % self.height
                c = (col + j - pattern_width//2) % self.width
                if self.grid[r, c] != pattern[i][j]:
                    return False
        return True
    
    def _record_patterns(self):
        """Record emerging patterns for AI learning"""
        # Record 3x3 patterns
        for row in range(self.height-2):
            for col in range(self.width-2):
                pattern = tuple(map(tuple, self.grid[row:row+3, col:col+3]))
                self.patterns[pattern] += 1
                
    def start(self):
        """Start simulation"""
        self.running = True
        self._animate()
        
    def stop(self):
        """Stop simulation"""
        self.running = False
        if self.after_id:
            self.canvas.after_cancel(self.after_id)
            
    def _animate(self):
        """Animate simulation"""
        if self.running:
            self.step()
            self.after_id = self.canvas.after(100, self._animate)

    def add_ai_rule(self, pattern: List[List[int]], result: int):
        """Allow AI to add custom rules based on observed patterns"""
        self.ai_rules.append({
            'pattern': pattern,
            'result': result,
            'uses': 0,
            'success_rate': 0.0
        })
        
    def _evaluate_ai_rules(self):
        """Evaluate effectiveness of AI-created rules"""
        for rule in self.ai_rules:
            if rule['uses'] > 0:
                # Calculate how often this rule led to interesting patterns
                pattern_score = sum(1 for p in self.patterns.values() 
                                 if p > 10) / len(self.patterns)
                rule['success_rate'] = pattern_score
                
        # Remove ineffective rules
        self.ai_rules = [r for r in self.ai_rules 
                        if r['success_rate'] > 0.3]

class AIVisualizationManager:
    """Manages overall visualization and evolution simulation"""
    
    def __init__(self, master):
        self.master = master
        self.renderer = None
        self.simulator = None
        
        # Create control panel
        self.controls = ttk.Frame(master)
        self.controls.pack(side=tk.TOP, fill=tk.X)
        
        # Add buttons
        ttk.Button(self.controls, text="Show IO Form", command=self._show_renderer).pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5)
        ttk.Button(self.controls, text="Evolution Simulation", command=self._show_simulator).pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5)
        
    def _show_renderer(self):
        """Show IO renderer window"""
        if not self.renderer:
            window = tk.Toplevel(self.master)
            window.title("Ileices Organism (IO)")
            self.renderer = IORenderer(window)
            self.renderer.canvas.pack(padx=10, pady=10)
            
    def _show_simulator(self):
        """Show evolution simulator window"""
        if not self.simulator:
            window = tk.Toplevel(self.master)
            window.title("Evolution Simulator")
            self.simulator = EvolutionSimulator(window)
            self.simulator.canvas.pack(padx=10, pady=10)
            
            # Add controls
            controls = ttk.Frame(window)
            controls.pack(fill=tk.X, padx=10, pady=5)
            
            ttk.Button(controls, text="Start", command=self.simulator.start).pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5)
            ttk.Button(controls, text="Stop", command=self.simulator.stop).pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5)

# Modify IleicesApp to include visualization
class IleicesApp(tk.Tk):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.title("Ileices - Firstborn AI")
        self.geometry("800x600")

        # AI Core
        self.dna = DigitalDNA()
        self.hpc_mode = tk.StringVar(value="Single Node")
        self.growth_factor_display = tk.StringVar(value=f"Growth: {self.dna.dna['growth_factor']:.2f}")

        # Add new managers
        self.resource_manager = ResourceManager()
        self.memory_manager = MemoryManager()
        self.templates = DataTemplates()
        self.ingestion_pipeline = DataIngestionPipeline()
        self.long_term_memory = LongTermMemory()
        self.screen_monitor = ScreenMonitor()
        self.excretion_manager = ExcretionManager(self.dna)
        self.global_hpc = GlobalHPC()
        self.account_system = AccountSystem()
        
        # Start background monitoring
        self.screen_monitor.start()

        # UI
        self._build_menu()
        self._build_main_frame()
        self._add_resource_controls()
        self._add_template_button()
        self._add_training_controls()
        self._add_upgrade_button()
        self._add_excretion_dashboard()
        self._add_hpc_controls()

        # Add visualization manager
        self.visualization = AIVisualizationManager(self)
        
    def _build_menu(self):
        menubar = tk.Menu(self)
        file_menu = tk.Menu(menubar, tearoff=0)
        file_menu.add_command(label="Spawn Super User Version", command=lambda: self.spawn_offspring("SuperUser"))
        file_menu.add_command(label="Spawn Paid User Version", command=lambda: self.spawn_offspring("PaidUser"))
        file_menu.add_command(label="Spawn Free User Version", command=lambda: self.spawn_offspring("FreeUser"))
        menubar.add_cascade(label="File", menu=file_menu)

        hpc_menu = tk.Menu(menubar, tearoff=0)
        hpc_menu.add_command(label="Single Node Mode", command=lambda: self.set_hpc_mode("Single Node"))
        hpc_menu.add_command(label="Global HPC Mode", command=lambda: self.set_hpc_mode("Global HPC"))
        menubar.add_cascade(label="HPC Mode", menu=hpc_menu)
        
        payment_menu = tk.Menu(menubar, tearoff=0)
        payment_menu.add_command(label="Set Credit Card", command=self.set_credit_card_info)
        menubar.add_cascade(label="Payments", menu=payment_menu)

        self.config(menu=menubar)

    def _build_main_frame(self):
        frame = tk.Frame(self)
        frame.pack(fill=tk.BOTH, expand=True)
        
        self.chat_display = tk.Text(frame, wrap=tk.WORD, height=15)
        self.chat_display.pack(fill=tk.BOTH, expand=True)
        
        self.user_input = tk.Entry(frame)
        self.user_input.pack(fill=tk.X)
        self.user_input.bind("<Return>", self.send_message)

        btn_frame = tk.Frame(frame)
        btn_frame.pack(fill=tk.X)
        
        send_btn = tk.Button(btn_frame, text="Send", command=self.send_message)
        send_btn.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5, pady=5)

        nurture_btn = tk.Button(btn_frame, text="Nurture AI", command=self.nurture_ai)
        nurture_btn.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=5, pady=5)
        
        self.hpc_label = tk.Label(btn_frame, textvariable=self.hpc_mode)
        self.hpc_label.pack(side=tk.RIGHT, padx=5, pady=5)
        
        self.growth_display = tk.Label(btn_frame, textvariable=self.growth_factor_display)
        self.growth_display.pack(side=tk.RIGHT, padx=5, pady=5)

        # Update renderer if exists
        if self.visualization.renderer:
            metrics = {
                'learning_rate': 0.001 * len(self.dna.memory),
                'complexity_gain': 0.001 * self.dna.dna['growth_factor']
            }
            self.visualization.renderer.update(metrics)
    
    async def send_message(self, event=None):
        """Enhanced message handling with excretion processing"""
        user_text = self.user_input.get().strip()
        if not user_text:
            return
            
        self._append_chat(f"You: {user_text}")
        self.user_input.delete(0, tk.END)
        
        response = self.dna.respond(user_text)
        self._append_chat(f"Ileices: {response}")
        
        # Process interaction through excretion pipeline
        processed = await self.dna.process_and_excrete({
            "input": user_text,
            "ai_response": response,
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat()
        })
        
        # Update dashboard
        self._update_excretion_dashboard(processed)

    def _append_chat(self, text):
        self.chat_display.insert(tk.END, text + "\n")
        self.chat_display.see(tk.END)

    def set_hpc_mode(self, mode):
        self.hpc_mode.set(mode)
        self._append_chat(f"* HPC mode switched to: {mode}")
    
    def nurture_ai(self):
        self.dna.mutate()
        self.growth_factor_display.set(f"Growth: {self.dna.dna['growth_factor']:.2f}")
        self._append_chat("* AI has evolved! *")

        # Update visualization
        if self.visualization.renderer:
            metrics = {
                'learning_rate': 0.01,
                'complexity_gain': 0.05
            }
            self.visualization.renderer.update(metrics)
    
    def spawn_offspring(self, version):
        filename = f"{version}.py"
        content = f"""#!/usr/bin/env python3\nprint('Spawned {version} version of Ileices.')"""
        with open(filename, "w") as f:
            f.write(content)
        self._append_chat(f"* Spawned {version} version of Ileices.")

        popup = tk.Toplevel(self)
        popup.title("Enter Payment Info")
        tk.Label(popup, text="Card Number:").pack()
        card_entry = tk.Entry(popup)
        card_entry.pack()
        tk.Label(popup, text="Expiry (MM/YY):").pack()
        expiry_entry = tk.Entry(popup)
